Use a **partial update**: send only the data that you want to update, leaving the rest intact.[2] The docs show this with an HTTP `PATCH` operation.

**Steps:**
1. Retrieve the stored data. Put that data in a Pydantic model.[1]
2. Generate a `dict` without default values from the input model (using `exclude_unset`).[1] This way you can update only the values actually set by the user, instead of overriding values already stored with default values in your model.[1]
3. Create a copy of the stored model, updating its attributes with the received partial updates (using the `update` parameter).[1]
4. Convert the copied model to something that can be stored in your DB (for example, using the `jsonable_encoder`).[1]
5. Save the data to your DB. Return the updated model.[1]

```python
@app.patch("/items/{item_id}")
async def update_item(item_id: str, item: Item) -> Item:
    stored_item_data = items[item_id]
    stored_item_model = Item(**stored_item_data)
    update_data = item.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
    updated_item = stored_item_model.model_copy(update=update_data)
    items[item_id] = jsonable_encoder(updated_item)
    return updated_item
```

**Important:** the input model is still validated. So, if you want to receive partial updates that can omit all the attributes, you need to have a model with all the attributes marked as optional (with default values or `None`).[1]

**With SQLModel:** after `exclude_unset=True`, we use `hero_db.sqlmodel_update(hero_data)` to update the `hero_db` with the data from `hero_data`.[4] The update model there (`HeroUpdate`) has all the same fields that would be needed to create a new hero, but all the fields are optional (they all have a default value).[5]

Also, you can actually use this same technique with an HTTP `PUT` operation.[1]

- https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/sql-databases/
